item.title: India’s Malhotra Says BRICS Eyeing Faster Cross-Border Payments
item.description: India is working to make cross-border payments easier and cheaper while promoting local-currency settlement with its trading partners, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said.

item.title: Yen Slides Toward 160 per Dollar, Raising Intervention Concerns
item.description: The yen was slightly weaker and approaching a key level against the dollar that could raise speculation Japanese authorities may intervene again to prop up the Japanese currency.

item.title: US Small-Business Optimism Rises to an Almost One-Year High
item.description: US small-business optimism rose in July to the highest level in almost a year as firms ramped up hiring plans and inflation pressures eased.

item.title: TPG Agrees to Buy South Korea’s Lotte Rental for $925 Million
item.description: TPG Capital has agreed to acquire a 61.2% stake in Lotte Rental Co. for 1.31 trillion won ($925 million), reviving a sale of South Korea’s largest car-rental company months after regulators blocked an earlier takeover.

item.title: Europe Is Ticking a Lot of Boxes for Investors Right Now
item.description: Earnings and economic growth turn out to be surprisingly robust.

item.title: Adani Lands $800 Million Data Center Loan as US Drops Charges
item.description: Indian conglomerate Adani Group has secured a loan of about $800 million from a group of overseas lenders to help fund its push into data centers, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: South African Unemployment Rate Jumps to Four-Year High of 33.6%
item.description: South Africa’s unemployment rate rose for a second successive quarter to a four-year high, potentially flagging fallout from the Iran war.

item.title: Emerging Assets Pressured as Higher Oil Stokes Inflation Worries
item.description: Most emerging-market currencies weakened and bond yields rose as fading chances of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz hit oil-sensitive assets around the globe.

item.title: Europe’s Faltering Defense Stocks Rally Is Tipped to Reignite
item.description: European defense stocks are set to deliver continued strong growth in the coming years as the region’s rearmament cycle enters a new stage, according to analysts at Barclays and RBC Capital Markets.

item.title: CoreWeave’s Forecast Is Key to Stopping Another Earnings Selloff
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. shares have been on a roll lately after a monthslong slump. Now, the neocloud provider’s earnings after the close Tuesday can give investors a sense of whether the rally is sustainable.

item.title: Apple's iPhone Manufacturing Adds to Growing India Supply Chain: Live Q&A
item.description: How Apple’s massive manufacturing expansion in India is reshaping the future of global technology supply chains, on Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 10:30am HKT, 8am IST.

item.title: DayOne Data Centers Is Said to Confidentially File for $5 Billion IPO in US
item.description: DayOne Data Centers has confidentially filed for a US initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: India Equity Fund Flows Ease in July as Small Caps Stay Hot
item.description: Flows into Indian equity funds moderated in July even as investors continued to pour money into small- and mid-cap strategies amid global headwinds including a spike in oil prices.

item.title: Resilient Europe Turns Into a Winning Bet for Money Managers
item.description: European markets are charging ahead this year, defying doom-laden forecasts that the Iran war would tip the region into stagflation.

item.title: Aerospace Engineer Puts Islamist-Led State Atop Budget Ranking
item.description: Terengganu, an oil-rich Malaysian state known for its conservative Islamist politics, topped a local think tank’s ranking for budget transparency under the leadership of aerospace engineer Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar.

item.title: Construction Giant L&T Said to Plan India Rare-Earth Magnet Bid
item.description: Larsen & Toubro Ltd. plans to manufacture rare-earth magnets in India, said people familiar with the matter, as the engineering giant rides a government push to reduce a reliance on imports and loosen China’s stranglehold over the critical industrial component.

item.title: Visma First-Half Annualized Revenue Rises 19% as Customer Base Surges
item.description: Norwegian business software provider Visma reported adjusted revenue growing by almost a fifth in the first half, helped by a jump in its customer base.

item.title: Uniper Targets Data Center Sales in UK, Germany on AI Demand
item.description: Uniper SE has identified about 10 sites across Europe that could be sold or leased for data-center development, as the German utility looks to capitalize on surging demand for AI infrastructure.

item.title: Wipro’s Nifty Exit Reflects Waning Clout of Indian IT Giants
item.description: Wipro Ltd.’s exit from India’s Nifty 50 to make way for exchange operator BSE Ltd. marks more than a benchmark reshuffle. It captures the shift from an outsourcing-led boom to one powered by the growing ranks of investors in the nation’s $5-trillion stock market.

item.title: India’s Banking Regulator Urges Lenders to Accelerate AI Spend
item.description: Indian lenders need to accelerate adoption of artificial intelligence by investing in technology and infrastructure besides training workers to upskill, central bank Governor Sanjay Malhotra said Tuesday.

item.title: BOK Deputy Governor Signals More Rate Hikes on Inflation Risk
item.description: The Bank of Korea will likely need to raise interest rates further as strong growth feeds into underlying inflation, its outgoing senior deputy governor said, while adding that the stronger currency and recent stock market moves give policymakers some flexibility in setting policy.

item.title: Aluminum Hits Seven-Week High as Hormuz Impasse Threatens Supply
item.description: Aluminum advanced for a seventh day as fading prospects for a quick deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz fueled concerns that Middle Eastern supplies would remain constrained for the foreseeable future.

item.title: Philippines Plans to Borrow $54 Billion in 2027 to Revive Growth
item.description: The Philippine government plans to borrow 3.3 trillion pesos ($54 billion) next year, up by a fifth, as it seeks to revitalize an economy rocked by the conflict in the Middle East and a corruption scandal.

item.title: Indonesia Copper Shipments Delayed by Gresik Smelter Outage
item.description: Copper shipments from Indonesia are suffering delays after the smelter that processes ore from the giant Grasberg mine was halted because of a boiler leak over the weekend.

item.title: VinSpace Signs Launch Pact With SpaceX for 2027 Mission
item.description: VinSpace Joint Stock Co., a unit of Vingroup, signed an agreement with SpaceX to launch its first satellites next year, as it seeks to build a domestic space business spanning satellite manufacturing, operations and data services.

item.title: RBA Holds Key Rate to Counter Elevated Inflation Pressures
item.description: Australia’s central bank kept its key interest rate unchanged on Tuesday, wagering that higher unemployment and a weakening property market will weigh on economic activity sufficiently to cool inflation.

item.title: Yuan’s Recent Calm May End on Seasonal Factors, Analysts Say
item.description: The yuan’s recent calm run may be nearing an end as September approaches, with typically strong fall exports and other seasonal factors expected to lift the Chinese currency, analysts say.

item.title: Hong Kong Tech Index Set for Overhaul With More Firms, AI Focus
item.description: Hong Kong’s main technology stock benchmark is set for a revamp to include more companies representing the fast-growing artificial intelligence and robotics sectors, a long‑awaited move for investors eager to better capture China’s technological advances.

item.title: Hong Kong May Expand Tax Breaks to Trading Firms, FT Says
item.description: Hong Kong regulators may include trading firms such as Jane Street and Citadel Securities in a sweeping new tax regime that has already boosted the city’s appeal to hedge funds, according to a report from the Financial Times.
